items: The summary form is cheap and safe to poll for monitoring
`IDLE` plus a consumer name is the standard stuck-work query
Delivery count rises on every claim or redelivery
Count above ~5 marks a poison message bound for a DLQ stream

slides.page_title: Acknowledgement and the Pending Entries List

items: Millions of unacked entries cost memory even after trimming
Trimming the stream does NOT remove PEL references
A trimmed entry still in the PEL becomes a phantom
`XCLAIM`/`XAUTOCLAIM` return that ID with a nil entry body

blocks.title: Redis 7.0 Cleanup
blocks.text: `XAUTOCLAIM` now deletes phantom IDs from the PEL and reports them in its third reply element. On 6.2 you clear them by hand with `XACK`.

blocks.q: Does a group process entries in order?
a_bullets: No — the PEL breaks strict ordering
A redelivered old entry can land after newer ones
Design handlers to tolerate out-of-order arrival

items: A dead consumer's pending entries are simply stranded
Nothing in Redis reassigns them automatically, ever
Recovery is an explicit application job you must write

lines: # JUSTID: no bodies, no retry increment

items: Transfers ownership of listed IDs idle past min-idle-time
min-idle-time is the safety interlock between racing rescuers
Only the first claim wins — it resets idle to 0
`JUSTID` is the cheap option for bulk ownership moves

rows: create PEL entry for unpending ID

slides.page_title: Recovering Stuck Work: XCLAIM and XAUTOCLAIM

items: 6.2+, scans the PEL and claims everything past the threshold
One call covers only COUNT entries — the rest stay stranded
One round trip beats `XPENDING` then `XCLAIM`
No risk of the ID list going stale between read and claim
Set min-idle-time well above your slowest legitimate job
Too low and you steal work from a consumer that is merely busy
Run the sweep from every worker on a 30s timer
A single leader sweeper is a single point of failure

lines: XACK orders g 1757-0   # leaves the PEL now

blocks.title: Scale-Down Hygiene
items: `XAUTOCLAIM ... JUSTID` for a fast rebalance
Skips bodies and skips retry increments
`DELCONSUMER` retired names only AFTER claiming away their PEL
Reverse that order and you destroy the pending work

slides.page_title: Recovering Stuck Work: XCLAIM and XAUTOCLAIM (cont.)

blocks.title: Dead-Letter Rule
blocks.text: When the delivery count crosses your limit, `XADD` the payload to `mystream:dlq`, then `XACK` the original. Ack last, so a crash mid-way retries instead of dropping.

items: Streams grow forever by default — no implicit cap exists
The #1 cause of Redis OOM in production event pipelines
At 1 KB per entry and 10k/sec, that is ~36 GB per hour
Decide retention before launch, not during the alert

lines: XADD s MAXLEN 1000 * k v      # exact, costly
XADD s MAXLEN ~ 1000 * k v    # node boundary
XADD s MAXLEN ~ 1000 LIMIT 100 * k v

items: Exact `MAXLEN` trims to roughly 1000 on every append
`~` stops at a macro-node boundary, so it keeps a few extra
`LIMIT n` caps work per call and is legal only with `~`
That bounds latency spikes when a huge backlog exists

caption.text: Part 3 of REDIS STREAMS & PUB/SUB. `PUBLISH` returning 2 does not mean two workers did the job — it means two sockets got the bytes, and Redis stopped caring. This ten-page field handbook walks the whole Redis messaging surface: why Pub/Sub loses messages six different ways, how consumer groups split work with XREADGROUP and the Pending Entries List, and how to rescue stuck entries with XAUTOCLAIM before your trim policy deletes work nobody ran. Save it before your next queue outage, not after.
